cards.explanation: The answer is the Wilderness of Sinai. The text says Israel entered the Wilderness of Sinai after leaving Rephidim, and camped there in front of the mountain (Exodus 19:2). Moses, Israel's leader, is about to do a LOT of walking up that mountain. Keep the name Sinai in your pocket, friends, because it's going to matter.

The answer is third. The text says they came to the Wilderness of Sinai "…on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt…" (Exodus 19:1) Same day of the month as the day they left, in the third month. Now THAT is a date worth circling.

The answer is eagles' wings. The LORD says, "You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself." (Exodus 19:4) It's a picture of being carried, and it ends with "to Myself." Not a bad ride, friends.
The answer is possession. The LORD says, "…you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations…" (Exodus 19:5) Treasured, friends. That's the kind of word you save for the good tray.
The answer is True! Right in the middle of His offer, the LORD says, "…for the whole earth is Mine." (Exodus 19:5) He's talking about all the nations and the whole earth. Every inch of it.

The answer is True, and the people answer together. Moses had set the words before the elders (Exodus 19:7). Then all the people answered together, "We will do everything that the LORD has spoken." (Exodus 19:8) That's a big yes, friends.

The answer is so the people hear Him speak with Moses. The LORD says, "…I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will always put their trust in you." (Exodus 19:9) The people get to hear it for themselves. I like a plan where everybody gets to listen in.

The answer is clothes. The LORD tells Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes" (Exodus 19:10) Clean clothes for the third day. I'd be rinsing my apron twice, friends.

The answer is that the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai. He says, "…on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people." (Exodus 19:11) That's why they're washing clothes and getting prepared. When the LORD says be ready, you get ready.

The answer is False, and the text is clear. The LORD says to tell the people, "Be careful not to go up on the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death." (Exodus 19:12) So the base is off limits just like the slopes. No touching, friends, not even a little.

The answer is True. After the punishment is laid out, the text adds, "…whether man or beast, he must not live." (Exodus 19:13) So the boundary around the mountain isn't only for people. Man or beast, the same rule applies. Even somebody's goat has to keep its hooves off.

The answer is the ram's horn. The LORD says, "Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain." (Exodus 19:13) That long blast is the signal, friends. Until then, you stay put.

The answer is True. Moses consecrated the people and they washed their clothes (Exodus 19:14). Then he said to them, "Be prepared for the third day…" (Exodus 19:15) Clean clothes first, then the heads-up. That's a leader who thinks ahead.

The answer is thunder and lightning. The text says, "On the third day, when morning came, there was thunder and lightning." (Exodus 19:16) And a thick cloud sat on the mountain too. Not a quiet morning, friends.

The answer is trembled. The text says the horn blast went out "…so that all the people in the camp trembled." (Exodus 19:16) Everybody in the camp, not just a few. That's a blast you feel in your knees.

The answer is that the LORD descended on it in fire. The text says, "Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire." (Exodus 19:18) The smoke comes from the LORD coming down. I've had smoke in my bakery before, friends, but that was just a forgotten batch, and all anybody did was open the windows.
The answer is furnace. The text says, "…the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace…" (Exodus 19:18) I know furnace smoke, friends. That's not a gentle puff.

The answer is False. The text says, "…as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder." (Exodus 19:19) God answered in the thunder, not in a whisper. That mountain was LOUD.

The answer is True. The LORD has just called Moses to the summit, and Moses goes up (Exodus 19:20). Then the LORD says to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) Up the mountain, then right back down again. I bet his legs have opinions.

The answer is perish. The LORD says to warn the people "…not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) It's a serious word for a serious moment, friends. The boundary is there for a reason.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them." (Exodus 19:22) The priests are named right there in His words. That little word "even" is doing real work.

The answer is that the LORD already had them set a boundary. Moses says to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’…" (Exodus 19:23) Moses is pointing back to what the LORD had already said. The boundary was the LORD's own instruction, friends.

The answer is Aaron. The LORD says, "Go down and bring Aaron with you." (Exodus 19:24) Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). The passage ends with Moses going down and speaking to the people (Exodus 19:25).
